items.chemoselectivity: The reaction demonstrates chemoselectivity by targeting the epoxide ring of cyclohexene oxide for nucleophilic ring-opening with NaOCN, without affecting other functional groups.
items.regioselectivity: The process shows moderate regioselectivity, with the cyanate ion (OCN-) attacking both tertiary carbons (C1 and C2) of cyclohexene oxide, as supported by docking studies. The enzyme HheG exhibits specificity for tertiary carbons in the symmetric cyclohexene oxide structure.
items.special_treatment: The process was scaled from analytical to pilot scale (10 L), achieving >90% conversion and 87% isolated yield. The reaction is self-regulated for pH (maintained at 10.5) using ethyl acetate as a co-solvent, eliminating the need for additional buffering agents. The process avoids toxic chemicals (e.g., sodium azide, NaBH4) and uses whole-cell biocatalysts. The product, trans-hexahydro-2(3H)-benzoxazolone (trans-HBC), was isolated as white crystals. The process is notable for its green chemistry approach and industrial scalability.
items.stereoselectivity: The reaction is stereoselective, producing the trans isomer of hexahydrobenzo[d]oxazol-2(3H)-one (trans-HBC) via SN2 attack, resulting in inversion at one carbon center. The product has an enantiomeric excess (ee) of 53%.
